title: Quantum Technology Atlas
description:
Every quantum-computing platform compared by the goal it serves — achievements, justified intentions and the most promising directions — followed by a technology graph of self-contained technologies across ten stack layers (carrier, encoding, gate mechanism, connectivity/transport, control, readout, code, decoder, interconnect, manufacturing), each on seven design attributes and connected by four edge types (requires/provides, alternatives, conflicts with mechanism–price–mitigation, dated defines), with the platform architectures as paths through the layers; a brief on every technology; and a register of every quantum machine built, announced or planned that the sources allow to be placed, each an architecture instance with graded evidence in every cell. An interactive web edition — the main page in English, in Russian and in Hebrew, with a page for every technology, machine, architecture and organisation — archived here as one zip of the site. Figures in the comparison, the graph section, the machines chapter and the briefs carry an evidence tag and trace to a dated, linked source; conflicts between sources are stated, not averaged.

Editions use calendar versioning; the concept DOI resolves to the newest edition. Data and build: https://github.com/qraveh/qt-map
notes: Interactive edition published at https://qodeh.com/publications/quantum-technology-atlas/. Research and drafting with Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction and review.
